sections.title: About this report
items: Customer: AnyCompany Health
Scope: 3 accounts
Collected: 2026-10-01 (point-in-time snapshot: changes made after this date are not reflected)
Reviewed: 29 buckets, about 218 PiB

sections.title: How to read this report

rows: Every bucket, which of the three risks it is protected from, and the recommended change. The Evidence column of the Excel download lists the settings behind each status.
The headline: protection counts per risk, critical exposures, AWS Backup posture, scope per account.
One row per bucket and action, sorted by severity. Filter by account or severity.
Buckets of the same workload configured differently across regions or accounts; always aligned to the stronger setting.
Why the gaps exist and what would keep them from coming back: maturity level, example rules, findings.
Cost quick wins and the cost of protection, with their order of magnitude and basis.

items: Three risks, three controls: human or application errors → Versioning · malicious activity → Object Lock · regional disruption → cross-region replication.
Coverage: protected · partial (for example versioning without Object Lock: recoverable, not immune) · unprotected (evidence shows the control is absent) · unconfirmed (the setting could not be read).

Row status: RISK GAP (a required protection is missing) · GAP — CONFIRM 3P (missing, but a backup tool may cover it) · PARTIAL · CONFIRM (required protection unreadable) · CONFIRM ROLE (the bucket role could not be determined) · PROTECTED · NON-PROD / LOG/TOOLING (not scored).
Priority focus: buckets to address first (risk + size + business criticality)

Example: a backup-tool bucket with versioning but no Object Lock is protected against human error and partial against malicious activity, status RISK GAP: for a backup target, protection against deliberate deletion is required, and versioned objects can still be permanently deleted.

sections.title: How the data was retrieved
items: Only configuration metadata was read, with the read-only credentials used for the scan: bucket settings, AWS Backup settings, daily S3 storage metrics (size and object count), S3 spend per region, IAM role names, CloudFormation stack names, AWS Config and Security Hub status.
No object was read, downloaded or listed. No setting was changed.

sections.title: How it works
items: Bucket roles are assigned from tags, account names, bucket names and replication / backup relationships (first match wins). Each role has an expected protection level (table below).
Buckets no rule can classify keep the role "unknown" (CONFIRM ROLE) and are not scored until their owner confirms the role.

Coverage comes from evidence only: an explicit "not configured" answer is unprotected; a setting that could not be read is unconfirmed, never unprotected. A stronger control that can't be verified never erases a verified weaker one (versioning with unreadable Object Lock stays partial).
Versioning is a prerequisite for Object Lock, replication and AWS Backup of S3: a bucket that never had versioning provably has none of them.
Critical exposures (10 in this report): production buckets failing two or more of backup coverage, point-in-time protection and delete protection, plus every backup target without immutability.

Priority score: +50 per missing required protection (+15 partial, +5 unconfirmed); size +30 (≥100 TiB), +20 (≥10 TiB), +12 (≥1 TiB), +5 (≥0.1 TiB); backup target or audit trail +15, production +8, non-production −30; business-critical naming (clinical, patient, customer, oracle, sql…) +10, non-production naming −15; a HIGH finding +10. Critical ≥80, High ≥60, Medium ≥35, else Low.

Versioning cost estimate: churn% × size per storage class × class price × (30-day noncurrent retention / 30). Churn basis: measured (request metrics), bounded (daily object-count drops + 1 point for overwrites) or prior (static 0%, append 1%, unknown 10% with a 2–25% range, high churn 25%). Only valid with a NoncurrentVersionExpiration rule.

Inconsistencies: buckets whose names match once region tokens, account IDs and replica suffixes are removed form a family (5 compared); differing settings are recommended up to the stronger value, never down.

sections.title: Limits
items: Configuration is not behaviour: the report shows what is enabled, not whether restores work or who can actually delete data.
Backup tools outside AWS Backup are detected from names and roles only; which buckets they cover is not known.
Without request metrics, write patterns and versioning costs are inferred from daily storage metrics; overwrites of the same key are invisible.
Not everything could be checked: 0 rows without a size, unconfirmed counts per check in the table above.
Costs are list-price estimates (US East (N. Virginia) list prices), before discounts, credits and taxes, labelled as estimates.
This is not an audit or a compliance attestation; regulatory retention and availability obligations need your own assessment.
Rules-based report: no generative AI was used.

rows: Keeps every version of an object. Enabled = on; Suspended = was on, old versions kept, new writes unprotected; never enabled = off.
An older version kept after an overwrite or delete. Billed like any object until a lifecycle rule expires it.
Write-once protection: a locked version cannot be deleted or overwritten until its retention date. Needs versioning.
Governance mode can be bypassed by users with a special permission; Compliance mode cannot be shortened by anyone, including the root user.
A default rule locks every new object; per-object retention is set by the writing application (for example a backup tool).
Requires a second factor to permanently delete versions or change versioning.
Cross-Region / Same-Region Replication: S3 copies new objects to another bucket. Only CRR protects against a regional disruption.
When on, a delete in the source also hides the object in the replica, so a replica alone is not a backup.
A plan schedules backups of selected resources; recovery points are stored in a vault.
Prevents recovery points in a vault from being deleted before their retention (Governance or Compliance mode).
An AWS Backup vault that is locked by default and shareable to a separate account for isolated recovery.
Per-region setting that lets AWS Backup protect S3. When off, backup plans silently skip buckets in that region.
Account- or bucket-level guardrail that overrides policies or ACLs granting public access.
Standard, Standard-IA, Intelligent-Tiering, Glacier Instant Retrieval, Glacier, Deep Archive: lower storage price, higher retrieval cost or delay.

sections.title: Next steps
items: Start with the critical exposures (Risk Review) and the priority focus buckets (Buckets).
Confirm the unconfirmed items and the assumptions with the bucket owners before planning changes.
Test configuration changes on a non-production bucket first, and add a NoncurrentVersionExpiration rule when enabling versioning.
Some changes are irreversible: Object Lock Compliance-mode retention cannot be shortened by anyone; start with Governance mode.

recommendations.title: 30 PiB in S3 Standard with no tiering: up to ~$465,000/month to save with Intelligent-Tiering
recommendations.description: All 30 PiB is billed at the Standard rate (estimate $706,600/month) and no lifecycle rule moves data to a cheaper class. The access pattern is not visible in configuration metadata, so confirm it. S3 Intelligent-Tiering is low-risk either way: it moves objects to Infrequent Access after 30 days and Archive Instant Access after 90 days without access, has no retrieval fees and keeps millisecond access. Worst case (everything read often): +~$15,000/month monitoring fee for 6B objects. If, as is typical for research datasets, ~70% of the data goes unread for 90+ days: ~$242,000/month instead of $706,600, saving up to ~$465,000/month (~$5.6M/year). One-time transition: ~$60,000.

tabs.label: Governance
tabs.summary: Governance maturity is assessed at level 2 of 5 (Repeatable), average 1.8. Strongest dimension: ownership & data classification. Weakest: preventive guardrails. The bucket fixes in this report close today's gaps; the governance items stop them from coming back.

levels.label: Ad hoc
levels.description: Protection is decided bucket by bucket by whoever creates it. No written standard; results depend on the team and the day.

levels.label: Repeatable
levels.description: Some teams reuse templates and protect well, but the rules are informal. Nothing verifies them, so drift goes unnoticed.

levels.label: Defined
levels.description: A written data protection standard maps each data class (e.g. legal, clinical, production) to required controls. IaC modules apply it by default and buckets carry classification tags.

levels.label: Managed
levels.description: Guardrails prevent weakening protection (SCPs, organization backup policies), detective controls cover every account, exceptions are recorded and time-boxed, and restores are tested.

levels.label: Optimized
levels.description: Compliance with the standard is measured continuously and reported to leadership, drift is remediated automatically, and recovery is exercised regularly from an isolated backup account.
